aboutScreen.title: About Orbit
aboutScreen.intro: Orbit is a workspace for AI agents, created to turn ideas into executable work. Chat, write code, research, test applications, and follow long-running tasks in one place. With memory, an integrated Browser, tools, Skills, and Workflows, Orbit helps you delegate complex work without losing control of the process.
aboutScreen.fraglab: Fragments Labs is an independent software lab building practical tools for developers, creators, and small teams. Its projects include tools like Orbit, Nodara and Fracta, each created to make technical work more accessible, automated, and efficient.

errorKind.moderation: The provider blocked this response with its content filter. This runs on the provider's servers and can't be turned off from here — it misfires often on turns that include images. Switching to another model resolves it.
errorKind.model-unavailable: This provider doesn't serve the selected model. Pick another model to continue.
errorKind.rate-limit: The provider hit its usage or request limit. Wait a bit or switch models.
errorKind.network: Network error talking to the provider (timeout, outage). Try again or switch models.
errorKind.context-length: The conversation grew past the model's context window, so the provider refused the request. Switching models won't help — compact the conversation or start a new one.
errorKind.context-length-turn: The work in this reply (tool results piling up across many steps) outgrew the model's context window. The conversation itself still fits, so compacting won't help: send a message asking it to continue — the new reply starts without this one's tool results.
errorKind.provider-config: This model's provider isn't ready: the API key is missing or the provider/SDK isn't available. Check Settings.

howtoScreen.title: How it works
howtoScreen.sectionModesDesc: Orbit offers several modes that change how the agent behaves. Turn them on before sending your message.
howtoScreen.tipText: Use the toggles below the input to quickly turn modes on/off, or the "+" button for advanced settings for Subagents, Vision, Orchestra, and Loop.

modes.label: Research
modes.description: Searches and reads web pages over HTTP.
modes.detail: Adds the websearch and webfetch tools to the agent. Fast for looking up docs and APIs.

modes.label: Browser
modes.description: Browses pages like a real browser.
modes.detail: Opens the right panel with a full browser. Runs JavaScript — ideal for SPAs and dynamic pages.

modes.label: Thinking
modes.detail: The model "thinks" before replying, producing deeper answers. Uses more tokens.

modes.label: Simple
modes.detail: Removes advanced formatting and tool blocks from the response.

modes.label: Memory (Brain)
modes.description: Orbit remembers facts and preferences across chats.
modes.detail: Adds memory tools. Orbit can save and recall facts automatically.

modes.label: Subagents
modes.detail: The agent delegates subtasks to background workers, discarded once the task ends.

modes.label: Orchestra
modes.description: Splits the request into a plan + persistent workers.
modes.detail: The orchestrator plans, you approve, and each task becomes a child session in the right panel.

modes.label: Loop
modes.description: Agent reviews and iterates until the task is done.
modes.detail: After each reply, the system reviews the result. If incomplete, the agent continues automatically.

modes.label: Plan Mode
modes.description: Read-only — produces a plan without editing.
modes.detail: Blocks write tools. The agent reads the code and produces a detailed plan.

modes.label: Permissions
modes.description: Security control over the agent's actions.

modes.label: Vision
modes.description: Delegates vision to a specific model.
modes.detail: While active, attached images are described by a configured vision model and only the text description enters the agent's context — never the image itself.

combos.label: Deep research
combos.description: The agent searches, browses dynamic pages, and reasons deeply. Ideal for investigating technical topics.

combos.label: Automatic refinement
combos.description: The agent reviews its own result with extended reasoning. Great for producing robust code.

combos.label: Orchestration with review
combos.description: Workers run in parallel and the loop reviews the result, creating follow-ups if needed.

combos.label: Workers on multiple fronts
combos.description: The orchestrator coordinates high-level tasks and each worker can use subagents for targeted investigations.

combos.label: Careful planning
combos.description: Before changing anything, the agent researches, reasons, and produces a plan without modifying files.

usageScreen.customHint: Pick a field above to choose a date.
usageScreen.noUsageInPeriod: No usage recorded in this period.
usageScreen.hoursByProjectInfo: The total estimates the combined working time (Orbit + you), not raw clock time. Orbit's generation time always counts. Your breaks enter with an inactivity margin: up to 30 min count in full (reading, testing or reviewing); 30–60 min count in full if you return with a detailed message; 1–1.5 h count only half, and only with a very long message. Longer breaks — or ones without a message that shows work — don't count.

pipeline.taskDescriptionHint: The full brief the phases receive — the task runs without a chat, so what is not here never reaches the agent.
pipeline.taskDependenciesHint: This task only starts after the selected ones are done.
pipeline.noTasksForDependency: No other task in this pipeline yet
pipeline.commitPromptHint: Prompt used by the agent that writes the final commit message. It receives the task, the notes from every phase, the changed files and the repository's most recent commit — exactly the same context a phase gets. Empty uses the default: what the task asks about the commit; with none, the style of the most recent commit; with no history, the memory preferences; and finally Conventional Commits (header + body of summarized topics).
pipeline.commitPromptEmpty: Empty = default prompt (task's request → most recent commit → memory → Conventional Commits).
pipeline.connectDesktop: Connect to Orbit Desktop to load the esteiras
pipeline.worktreePerTask: Isolate each task in a worktree
pipeline.worktreePerTaskHint: Each task works on its own branch and copy, and its work is merged into one integration branch of the pipeline. Applies to tasks that haven't started yet.
pipeline.noGitNotice: Pipelines were designed to work with git and worktrees. This folder has no git, so tasks run one at a time in your folder and there is nothing to merge. Initialize git in it to get the full flow.
pipeline.worktreeOffNotice: Pipelines work much better with worktrees: tasks run in isolation, in parallel, and their work is merged for you. Without them, tasks run one at a time in your folder.
pipeline.commitOffNotice: Recommended: commit per task. Each task's work stays traceable; without commits, changes pile up in the working tree.
pipeline.commitOffSharedNotice: Recommended: commit per task. Without commits, tasks run one at a time in the pipeline's worktree and their changes pile up there until you merge.
pipeline.parallelTasksHint: How many automatic tasks run at once. Each one has its own worktree and they are merged one at a time.

merge.hint: Moves {{branch}} to the integration branch. Nothing is pushed.
merge.simpleMode: Simple mode: tasks run in your folder, nothing is merged.
merge.blocked: {{branch}} is checked out at {{where}} with uncommitted changes in: {{files}}. Commit or stash them and merge again.
merge.dirtyBody: The integration worktree has changes that are not committed. Commit them (the pipeline model writes the message) to continue, or cancel.
